response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS a FROM film GROUP BY rating), o AS (SELECT AVG(length) AS overall FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL), c1 AS (SELECT r.rating, r.a FROM r, o WHERE r.a > o.overall), m AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS mean_all FROM r), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS mean_c1 FROM c1), c2 AS (SELECT c1.rating, c1.a FROM c1, m WHERE c1.a > m.mean_all) SELECT AVG(c2.a) AS mean_avg_length, AVG(c2.a - o.overall) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(c2.a - m1.mean_c1) AS avg_above_first_cut_mean FROM c2, o, m1

assumptions.assumption: 'Longer than average' in the first cut means above the overall average length across all films (non-null lengths), not the mean of the rating averages.
'The mean of their own average lengths' is the unweighted mean of the average lengths of all 5 ratings. The 'first average' used for the gap is the overall film average from the first cut.

alternatives.interpretation: The first cut compares each rating's average to the unweighted mean of all ratings' averages, and the second cut compares the survivors to the mean of the first-cut survivors' averages. The gap is measured against the first cut's mean.
